about: Ready-made four-person poster recipes written by Claude. Copy a film's menu straight into its edition block. Do not edit this file.

s.note: Warm blini with crème fraîche, smoked salmon, salmon roe and dill.
s.how: Warm 16 cocktail blini on a tray at 180C for 4 minutes. Top each with 1 tsp crème fraîche, a curl of smoked salmon (about 150g in total), 1/2 tsp salmon roe and a small sprig of dill. Pass around on a tray straight away so the blini are still warm.

s.note: Cashews and almonds roasted with butter, rosemary, brown sugar and cayenne.
s.how: Melt 30g butter with 1 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp chopped rosemary, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper and 1/2 tsp salt. Toss through 150g cashews and 150g almonds, spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring halfway. Cool for 5 minutes so they crisp, then serve warm in a glass bowl.

m.note: Shaved rare roast beef in soft rolls with horseradish cream and rocket.
m.how: Rub a 1kg beef topside with 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp cracked pepper and 1 tsp salt. Roast at 200C for about 35 minutes until 52C inside, then rest 15 minutes and shave thin. Stir 2 tbsp horseradish into 150ml sour cream. Split 8 soft rolls, spread with the horseradish cream and fill with beef, 60g rocket and 100g pickled onions, sliced.

w.note: Vanilla sponge fingers split and piped with fluffy marshmallow cream.
w.how: Beat 125g soft butter with 150g caster sugar, add 3 eggs one at a time and 1 tsp vanilla extract, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 80ml milk. Bake in a lined 20 by 30cm tin at 180C for 22 minutes, cool and cut into 12 fingers. For the cream, boil 150g caster sugar with 50ml water to 118C and pour into 2 egg whites whisking hard until thick and glossy. Split the fingers and pipe the cream inside.

d.note: Bourbon over one big ice cube with a strip of orange peel.
d.how: Put one large ice cube in each of four heavy tumblers. Pour 45ml bourbon over each, about 180ml in total. Peel 4 wide strips of orange zest, twist each over a glass to release the oil and drop it in. Serve straight away.

s.note: Golden chickpea fritters fried crisp, finished with lemon and salt.
s.how: Whisk 250g chickpea flour into 750ml cold water with 1 tsp salt until smooth. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes until very thick. Add 2 tbsp chopped parsley, spread 1cm thick on an oiled tray and leave to set for 1 hour. Cut into squares and fry in 180C oil until puffed and golden. Drain, salt, and serve with lemon wedges.

s.note: Ripe rockmelon wedges draped with prosciutto, pepper and olive oil.
s.how: Leave 1 rockmelon at room temperature for an hour. Halve, scoop out the seeds, cut into 12 long wedges and cut off the skin. Drape each wedge with a slice of prosciutto (about 150g in total), add a crack of black pepper and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil just before serving.

m.note: Rigatoni with fried eggplant, tomato and basil, under grated ricotta salata.
m.how: Cut 2 eggplants into thick half moons and fry in batches in 120ml olive oil until deep gold, drain. Fry 3 sliced garlic cloves in 2 tbsp of the oil, add 800g San Marzano tomatoes and a handful of basil, simmer 20 minutes and season. Cook 500g rigatoni until al dente, toss with the sauce, eggplant and a splash of pasta water. Grate 100g ricotta salata heavily over the top.

w.note: Crisp shells filled with sweet ricotta, candied orange and pistachio.
w.how: Drain 500g fresh ricotta in a sieve for 2 hours. Beat with 80g icing sugar, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon and 40g finely chopped candied orange peel. Spoon into a piping bag and fill 8 cannoli shells just before serving. Dip each end in 30g chopped pistachios and dust with a little more icing sugar.

d.note: Sicilian red opened early and served at cellar temperature.
d.how: Open one 750ml bottle of Nero d'Avola 30 minutes before dinner and keep it at about 16C, cooler than the room. Pour into four large glasses, about 180ml each, with no ice.

s.note: Buttery potato and slow-cooked onion baked in golden puff pastry.
s.how: Boil 500g peeled potatoes 15 minutes, drain and mash. Cook 1 finely diced brown onion in 30g butter over low heat for 15 minutes until golden, then mix into the mash with salt and white pepper. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into 4 squares each, fill, fold into parcels and brush with 1 beaten egg. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 40g hot English mustard.

s.note: Thin baked bagel crisps with chive cream cheese and smoked salmon.
s.how: Slice 3 day-old bagels into thin rounds, brush with 2 tbsp olive oil and bake at 180C for 12 minutes until crisp. Beat 250g cream cheese with 2 tbsp chopped chives and the zest of 1 lemon. Serve the crisps with the schmear and 150g smoked salmon on the side.

m.note: Slow-braised brisket on sweet onions, sliced thick with rich gravy.
m.how: Season a 1.5kg beef brisket with salt and pepper and sear hard on all sides. Slice 3 brown onions into a roasting dish, sit the brisket on top, and pour over 500ml beef stock whisked with 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 tsp sweet paprika. Cover and braise at 150C for 4 hours. Rest 20 minutes, slice against the grain, and boil the juices for 10 minutes to make gravy.

w.note: Sponge cups piped high with vanilla cream and a cherry.
w.how: Cut 8 rounds from a 300g sponge cake to fit the bottom of 8 paper cups. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 100g mascarpone, 2 tbsp icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla extract to firm peaks. Pipe high over the sponge in a tall swirl and top each with a maraschino cherry. Chill 30 minutes before serving.

d.note: Rye whiskey poured neat into china coffee cups.
d.how: Pour 45ml rye whiskey, about 180ml in total, into each of four china coffee cups, the way it was served when it was illegal. Put a small jug of cold water on the table so everyone can add a splash.

s.note: Grilled ciabatta with tomato and garlic sliced as thin as possible.
s.how: Slice 6 garlic cloves paper thin on a mandoline and cook in 80ml extra virgin olive oil over low heat for 5 minutes until soft and barely golden. Grill 8 slices of ciabatta, rub with the cut side of 2 halved tomatoes and season with salt. Spoon the garlic and its oil over the top and finish with torn basil.

s.note: Poached prawns on crisp iceberg with a brandy Marie Rose sauce.
s.how: Poach 500g peeled green prawns for 2 minutes in salted water with a slice of lemon, then chill in iced water. Mix 120g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, a few drops of hot sauce and 1 tsp brandy. Shred half an iceberg lettuce into four coupes, add the prawns and spoon over the sauce. Dust with paprika and serve with lemon wedges.

m.note: Veal, beef and pork meatballs simmered in a thin-garlic tomato sauce.
m.how: Soak 2 slices bread in 80ml milk, then mix with 200g veal mince, 200g beef mince, 200g pork mince, 1 egg, 40g grated pecorino, chopped parsley and 1 crushed garlic clove. Roll into 16 balls and brown. In the same pot gently cook 4 garlic cloves sliced razor thin and half a diced onion, add 800g San Marzano tomatoes and the meatballs and simmer 90 minutes. Serve over 500g spaghetti.

w.note: Fluffy scraped lemon ice served in little paper cups.
w.how: Simmer 200g caster sugar with 500ml water and the zest of 2 lemons for 5 minutes, then cool. Stir in 250ml lemon juice, about 6 lemons. Pour into a shallow tray and freeze, scraping with a fork every 30 minutes for 3 hours until light and fluffy. Serve in paper cups.

d.note: Blended Scotch over ice in a tall glass, topped with soda.
d.how: Fill four highball glasses with ice. Pour 45ml blended Scotch into each, about 180ml in total, and top with chilled soda water, about 120ml each. No garnish, the way it was poured at the Bamboo Lounge.

s.note: Saffron rice balls filled with beef ragù, peas and mozzarella.
s.how: Cook 300g arborio rice in 900ml stock with a pinch of saffron until thick, stir in 40g parmesan and chill overnight on a tray. Brown 150g beef mince with 50g frozen peas and 2 tbsp passata. Wrap golf balls of rice around a spoon of filling and a cube of mozzarella. Roll in flour, 2 beaten eggs and 100g breadcrumbs, and fry at 175C until deep gold.

s.note: Pressed slider rolls of ham, mojo pork, Swiss cheese and pickle.
s.how: Split 8 slider rolls and smear the cut sides with 2 tbsp yellow mustard. Layer with 150g leg ham, 150g sliced roast pork, 8 slices Swiss cheese and sliced dill pickles. Brush the tops with 30g melted butter and press in a heavy pan over medium heat with a second pan on top, 3 minutes a side, until the cheese melts.

m.note: Baked ziti with sausage tomato sauce, seasoned ricotta and blistered mozzarella.
m.how: Squeeze 500g Italian sausages from their skins and brown, add 700ml passata and simmer 30 minutes. Cook 500g ziti or penne 3 minutes short of done. Mix 400g ricotta with 50g grated parmesan, nutmeg and parsley. Layer pasta, sauce and ricotta in a baking dish, top with 200g torn mozzarella and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until blistered.

w.note: Vanilla slab cake iced pale green and cut like an island.
w.how: Beat 200g soft butter with 200g caster sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour with 100ml milk. Bake in a lined slab tin at 180C for 30 minutes and cool. Trim into a rough island shape. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar and a few drops of green food colouring, spread thinly then again, pipe happy birthday across and slice at the table.

d.note: White rum, fresh lime and sugar shaken hard and served ice cold.
d.how: Make sugar syrup by dissolving 60g caster sugar in 60ml hot water and cooling. For each drink shake 60ml white rum, 25ml fresh lime juice and 15ml syrup hard with plenty of ice, then double strain into a chilled coupe. Makes four, with 240ml rum and about 4 limes.

s.note: Flaky pastry cases with a silky just-set egg custard.
s.how: Dissolve 70g caster sugar in 120ml hot water and cool. Whisk in 3 eggs, 80ml evaporated milk and 40ml full cream milk, then strain. Cut 12 rounds from 2 sheets puff pastry and press into a greased patty tin. Fill three quarters full and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble.

s.note: Crisp salt and pepper prawns tossed with fried garlic and chilli.
s.how: Dry 500g shell-on green prawns well, season with salt and white pepper and toss in 60g potato starch. Fry in batches at 190C for 2 minutes until crisp. In a wok, fry 4 sliced garlic cloves, 1 sliced red chilli and 2 sliced spring onions in a little oil for 30 seconds, add the prawns and toss well.

m.note: Five spice roast duck with lacquered skin, plum sauce and rice.
m.how: Rub the cavity of a 2kg whole duck with 2 tsp five spice and 1 tsp salt, and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight to dry the skin. Brush with 2 tbsp honey loosened with hot water and roast at 180C for 90 minutes, brushing again twice. Rest 15 minutes and chop through the bone. Serve with 150ml plum sauce and 2 cups jasmine rice.

w.note: Chilled mango and coconut cream with sago pearls and pomelo.
w.how: Boil 80g sago pearls in plenty of water for 15 minutes until clear, then rinse under cold water and chill. Blend the flesh of 2 mangoes with 200ml coconut milk and 100ml evaporated milk. Fold in the sago, divide into bowls and top with diced mango from a third mango and segments of half a pomelo.

d.note: Strong black tea strained smooth with evaporated milk and sugar.
d.how: Simmer 4 tbsp loose black tea in 800ml water for 5 minutes. Strain twice through a fine cloth or sieve for a smooth tea. Add 200ml evaporated milk and 4 tsp caster sugar, stir, and serve hot or poured over ice.

s.note: Lacy salt cod fritters with garlic and coriander.
s.how: Soak 250g salt cod for 24 hours, changing the water three times, then flake. Whisk 200g plain flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 300ml water, 2 crushed garlic cloves and a handful of chopped coriander into a loose batter and fold in the cod. Fry wide flat spoonfuls in 180C oil until golden and lacy, drain and salt.

s.note: Twice-fried smashed green plantain with garlic and lime mojo.
s.how: Peel 3 green plantains and cut into 3cm chunks. Fry at 160C for 4 minutes until soft, smash flat with a heavy glass and fry again at 190C until crisp. Salt well. Mix 3 crushed garlic cloves with the juice of 2 limes and 60ml olive oil and spoon over.

m.note: Garlic and oregano roast pork shoulder with crackling, rice and pigeon peas.
m.how: Stab a 2kg pork shoulder all over and rub with 8 crushed garlic cloves, 2 tsp dried oregano, 2 tsp salt and 2 tbsp white vinegar. Marinate overnight. Roast skin up at 160C for 5 hours, then 230C for 20 minutes to crackle. Cook 400g long grain rice with a 400g tin of pigeon peas, stock and a little onion to serve alongside.

w.note: Coconut caramel flan, baked slowly and turned out cold.
w.how: Melt 150g caster sugar in a pan until deep amber and pour into a ring tin. Blend a 395g tin condensed milk, 270ml coconut milk, 375ml evaporated milk and 5 eggs and pour over the caramel. Bake in a water bath at 160C for 50 minutes until just set. Chill overnight, run a knife around and turn out onto a plate.

d.note: Golden rum over ice with cold cola and a big squeeze of lime.
d.how: Fill four tall glasses with ice. Pour 45ml golden rum into each, about 180ml in total, top with cold cola and squeeze in a big wedge of lime, about 2 limes for four drinks.

s.note: Clams under golden garlic, oregano and parmesan crumbs.
s.how: Steam 1kg clams with a splash of water in a covered pan until they open, about 4 minutes, and discard any closed ones. Remove the top shells. Mix 60g breadcrumbs, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tsp dried oregano, 30g grated parmesan and 3 tbsp olive oil. Top each clam and grill for 3 minutes until golden.

s.note: Prosciutto on rockmelon, with bocconcini dressed in bright basil oil.
s.how: Cut 1 rockmelon into 12 skinless wedges and drape with 120g prosciutto. Blitz a bunch of basil with 80ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Drain 220g bocconcini, dress with the basil oil and cracked pepper and serve beside the melon.

m.note: Seared veal escalopes in a glossy mushroom and marsala sauce.
m.how: Dust 600g veal escalopes in seasoned flour and sear in butter and oil for 1 minute a side, then set aside. Brown 250g sliced button mushrooms in the same pan, add 150ml marsala and 150ml beef stock and reduce by half. Whisk in 40g cold butter, return the veal and warm through for a minute. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Warm whisked marsala custard spooned over fresh strawberries.
w.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks, 60g caster sugar and 80ml marsala in a heatproof bowl over simmering water for 6 to 8 minutes until thick, pale and tripled in volume. Spoon warm over 250g halved strawberries in four glasses and serve straight away.

d.note: Chianti Classico decanted and poured with a flourish.
d.how: Decant one 750ml bottle of Chianti Classico 30 minutes before dinner and keep it at about 16C. Pour into four glasses, about 180ml each, the way Charlie would at the restaurant.

s.note: Blistered Italian sausage with charred onion and capsicum on toothpicks.
s.how: Grill 500g Italian sausages over high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until blistered and cooked through. Grill 1 red capsicum and 1 onion cut into chunks until charred at the edges. Slice the sausages thick and thread onto toothpicks with the capsicum and onion. Serve with 50g hot mustard.

s.note: Tender squid rings in a crisp semolina coat with lemon.
s.how: Slice 500g squid tubes into rings and soak in 250ml buttermilk for 30 minutes. Mix 100g fine semolina with 100g plain flour and plenty of salt. Drain the squid, toss in the flour mix and fry in 190C oil in batches for 90 seconds until pale gold. Salt and serve with 2 lemons cut into wedges.

m.note: Penne in a fiery garlic, chilli and tomato sauce with pecorino.
m.how: Gently fry 4 sliced garlic cloves and 1 tsp dried chilli flakes in 4 tbsp olive oil for 2 minutes. Add 800g crushed tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes, seasoning well. Cook 500g penne until al dente and toss through the sauce with a splash of pasta water and chopped parsley. Finish with 50g grated pecorino.

w.note: Hot fried dough puffs shaken in a bag of icing sugar.
w.how: Mix 250g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp caster sugar, a pinch of salt and 200ml warm water into a sticky batter and leave to rise for 1 hour. Drop teaspoons into 175C oil and fry 3 minutes until puffed and golden. Drain, tip into a paper bag with 60g icing sugar, shake and eat hot.

d.note: Cheap and cheerful Italian red in a jug, slightly chilled.
d.how: Chill one 750ml bottle of Italian red in the fridge for 20 minutes so it is just cool. Pour into a jug and serve in short tumblers, about 180ml each.

s.note: Chilled prawns on iceberg with horseradish Marie Rose.
s.how: Poach 500g peeled green prawns in salted water with lemon and a bay leaf for 2 minutes, then chill in iced water. Mix 120g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp horseradish and a squeeze of lemon. Shred half an iceberg lettuce into four glasses, hang the prawns off the rims and spoon the sauce into the middle.

s.n: Card table chips and onion dip
s.note: Thick-cut chips with a deep caramelised onion and chive dip.
s.how: Cook 2 thinly sliced brown onions in 2 tbsp oil over low heat for 40 minutes until deep brown, then cool. Mix with 200g sour cream, 100g cream cheese, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tbsp chopped chives and salt. Serve with two 175g bags of thick-cut potato chips.

m.note: Butter-basted rib eye with thyme and garlic, and creamed spinach.
m.how: Salt 2 rib eye steaks, about 400g each, and leave uncovered on a rack in the fridge overnight. Sear in a smoking pan for 3 minutes a side, then add 50g butter, 4 sprigs thyme and 3 crushed garlic cloves and baste until 54C inside. Rest 8 minutes and slice. Wilt 500g spinach, squeeze dry and simmer with 150ml thickened cream and nutmeg.

w.note: Buttermilk muffins with exactly ten blueberries pressed into each.
w.how: Whisk 300g plain flour, 150g caster sugar and 2 tsp baking powder. Mix 2 eggs, 250ml buttermilk and 90g melted butter, then fold into the dry mix until just combined. Spoon into 12 lined muffin cases and press exactly 10 blueberries into the top of each. Bake at 190C for 20 minutes.

d.note: Gin stirred with a little vermouth, served in a frozen glass.
d.how: Freeze four martini glasses for 30 minutes. For each drink stir 60ml gin with 10ml dry vermouth over plenty of ice for 30 seconds and strain into a frozen glass. Garnish with a green olive on a pick. Makes four with 240ml gin and 40ml vermouth.

s.note: Crisp-bottomed pork dumplings with chilli oil and black vinegar.
s.how: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan and add 24 frozen pork dumplings flat side down. Fry 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden, add 120ml water, cover and steam 6 minutes until the water is gone. Fry 1 more minute to re-crisp. Mix 3 tbsp black vinegar with 1 tbsp chilli oil and sliced spring onion for dipping.

s.note: Charred garlic, chilli and lime prawn skewers with sweet chilli dip.
s.how: Peel 16 king prawns, leaving the tails on, and toss with 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 chopped red chilli, the zest and juice of 1 lime and 2 tbsp oil. Thread onto 8 skewers and grill 2 minutes a side until pink and charred. Serve on ice with 100ml sweet chilli sauce and lime wedges.

m.note: Thick wok-fried noodles with pork, cabbage, carrot and oyster sauce.
m.how: Slice 400g pork shoulder thin and toss with 1 tbsp soy sauce. Stir-fry in a smoking wok with 2 tbsp oil for 3 minutes. Add a quarter of a cabbage, shredded, and 1 carrot cut into matchsticks, stir-fry 2 minutes. Add 800g fresh udon, 3 tbsp oyster sauce, 2 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tbsp Shaoxing wine, toss until glossy and finish with sliced spring onion.

w.note: Blue tea jelly over coconut panna cotta that turns purple with lemon.
w.how: Warm 300ml coconut milk with 60g caster sugar, add 2 softened gelatine leaves, pour into four glasses and chill 2 hours. Steep 2 tbsp dried butterfly pea flowers in 300ml boiling water for 5 minutes, strain, stir in 40g sugar and 2 softened gelatine leaves, cool and pour over. Chill 3 hours. Squeeze lemon on top at the table and watch it turn purple.

d.note: Gin and dry vermouth stirred ice cold with an olive.
d.how: Chill four martini glasses in the freezer for 30 minutes. For each drink, stir 60ml gin with 10ml dry vermouth over plenty of ice for 30 seconds and strain into a cold glass. Add a green olive on a pick. Makes four with 240ml gin and 40ml vermouth.

s.note: Butterflied prawns sizzled with garlic, chilli, white wine and butter.
s.how: Butterfly 500g green prawns. Heat 3 tbsp olive oil until very hot, add the prawns with 4 sliced garlic cloves and a pinch of chilli flakes and cook 2 minutes. Add 80ml white wine, bubble for a minute, then swirl in 30g butter and chopped parsley. Serve in the pan with crusty bread for the juices.

s.note: Golden crumbed mozzarella fingers with warm tomato sauce to dip.
s.how: Cut 400g low-moisture mozzarella into 16 fingers and freeze 20 minutes. Dip in 50g flour, then 2 beaten eggs, then 100g breadcrumbs, then egg and crumbs again. Fry at 180C for 90 seconds until golden. Warm 250ml passata with a pinch of salt and oregano for dipping.

m.note: Seared sirloin brushed with sticky teriyaki, with rice and greens.
m.how: Simmer 80ml soy sauce, 80ml mirin, 60ml sake and 2 tbsp sugar for 5 minutes until syrupy. Sear 4 sirloin steaks, about 800g, in a smoking pan for 3 minutes a side, brushing with glaze in the last minute. Rest 5 minutes and slice. Serve with 400g steamed short grain rice and 4 blanched bok choy.

w.note: Light baked ricotta cheesecake with lemon and vanilla.
w.how: Drain 750g fresh ricotta in a sieve for 2 hours. Beat with 150g caster sugar, 4 eggs, the zest of 1 lemon and 1 tsp vanilla extract until smooth. Pour into a lined 22cm springform tin and bake at 160C for 60 minutes. Turn off the oven and cool inside with the door ajar. Dust with icing sugar to serve.

d.note: Blended Scotch over one big ice cube in a heavy tumbler.
d.how: Put a single large ice cube in each of four heavy tumblers. Pour 45ml blended Scotch over each, about 180ml in total. Serve straight away, no garnish.

s.note: Pizza dough knots tossed hot in garlic butter and parmesan.
s.how: Cut 500g pizza dough into 12 strips, tie each into a loose knot and leave to prove 30 minutes on a lined tray. Bake at 230C for 12 minutes until golden. Melt 50g butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves and toss the knots in it straight from the oven, then shower with 30g grated parmesan.

s.note: Crisp fries under hot beef gravy and melted mozzarella.
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into chips, soak 30 minutes, dry and fry at 150C for 6 minutes, then at 190C until crisp. Melt 30g butter, stir in 2 tbsp flour for a minute, then whisk in 400ml hot beef stock and simmer 5 minutes into gravy. Pile the fries on a tray, pour over the gravy, top with 150g grated mozzarella and grill for a minute.

m.note: Big thin New York slices, stacked two at a time and folded.
m.how: Take 2 balls of pizza dough, about 500g, rested at room temperature for an hour. Blend 400g crushed tomatoes with 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp dried oregano. Stretch each base thin, spread with sauce and scatter 250g grated low-moisture mozzarella across both. Bake on a preheated tray at the oven's highest setting for 8 to 10 minutes. Cut into big slices, stack two and fold.

w.note: Cake and cream cheese balls dipped in white chocolate and silver cachous.
w.how: Crumble 400g butter cake into a bowl and mix with 100g cream cheese until it holds together. Roll into 16 balls and chill 30 minutes. Push a stick into each, dip in 300g melted white chocolate and roll in 50g silver cachous so they sparkle. Stand in a glass to set.

d.note: Blended whiskey over ice topped with lemonade.
d.how: Fill four tall glasses with ice. Pour 45ml blended whiskey into each, about 180ml in total, then top with chilled lemonade, about 150ml a glass. Stir once and serve.

s.note: Poppy seed buns loaded Chicago style with relish, pickle and celery salt.
s.how: Simmer 8 all-beef franks for 5 minutes, then griddle until marked. Steam 8 poppy seed hot dog buns for a minute. Load each frank with yellow mustard, sweet relish, diced onion, tomato wedges, a pickle spear and 2 pickled chillies, and finish with a pinch of celery salt. No tomato sauce.

s.note: Soft salted pretzels with a honey and lager mustard.
s.how: Mix 500g bread flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tsp salt and 300ml warm water, knead 8 minutes and rise 1 hour. Shape 8 pretzels. Dip each for 30 seconds in 2 litres boiling water with 4 tbsp bicarb soda, sprinkle with rock salt and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Whisk 4 tbsp wholegrain mustard with 2 tbsp lager and 1 tbsp honey.

m.note: Shaved roast beef soaked in garlic jus, piled in rolls with giardiniera.
m.how: Rub a 1kg beef topside with salt, pepper and oregano and roast at 200C to 52C inside, about 35 minutes. Chill, then shave thin. Simmer 750ml beef stock with 3 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tsp dried oregano and plenty of black pepper. Warm the beef in the jus, pile into 4 long rolls, dip the whole sandwich, and top with 200g hot giardiniera.

w.note: Glossy bourbon pecan filling baked in crisp sweet shortcrust.
w.how: Line a 23cm tin with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust pastry, blind bake at 180C for 15 minutes. Whisk 3 eggs, 200ml golden syrup, 100g brown sugar, 60g melted butter and 30ml bourbon, then fold in 200g pecans. Pour into the case and bake at 170C for 45 minutes until just set. Cool before slicing.

d.note: Rye stirred with sugar and bitters over a big cube.
d.how: Make sugar syrup by dissolving 40g caster sugar in 40ml hot water. For each drink, stir 60ml rye whiskey, 10ml syrup and 2 dashes aromatic bitters over ice for 30 seconds and strain over one big cube. Twist a strip of orange peel over the top. Makes four with 240ml rye.

s.note: Creamy serrano ham croquettes with a crisp golden crumb.
s.how: Melt 60g butter, stir in 70g plain flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in 500ml warm milk and cook 8 minutes until very thick. Stir in 100g finely chopped serrano ham and a pinch of nutmeg. Spread on a tray, cover and chill overnight. Roll into 16 logs, dip in 2 beaten eggs and 100g fine breadcrumbs, and fry at 180C until golden.

s.note: Twice-fried smashed green plantain under garlic lime mojo.
s.how: Peel 3 green plantains, cut into 3cm chunks and fry at 160C for 4 minutes until soft. Smash flat with a heavy glass and fry again at 190C until crisp. Mix 3 crushed garlic cloves, the juice of 2 limes and 60ml olive oil, spoon over and finish with flaky salt.

m.note: Shredded flank steak in tomato sofrito with olives, rice and black beans.
m.how: Simmer 1kg flank steak with 2 bay leaves and half an onion in water for 2 hours until tender, then shred, keeping 250ml broth. Fry 1 sliced onion, 2 sliced capsicums and 3 garlic cloves until soft, add 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano, 400g crushed tomatoes, 80g green olives, the beef and broth and simmer 20 minutes. Serve with 300g rice and 2 tins black beans.

w.note: Flaky puff pastry parcels of guava paste and cream cheese.
w.how: Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into 4 squares each. Put a 30g slice of guava paste and a teaspoon of cream cheese in the middle of 4 squares, using 120g guava and 100g cream cheese in total. Cover with the other squares, press the edges with a fork, brush with 1 beaten egg and sprinkle with sugar. Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed.

d.note: White rum, lime and mint over crushed ice, topped with soda.
d.how: Dissolve 60g caster sugar in 60ml hot water and cool. For each drink, gently muddle 8 mint leaves with 20ml syrup and 25ml lime juice in a tall glass, add 50ml white rum and fill with crushed ice. Top with soda water and stir. Makes four with 200ml rum and about 4 limes.

s.note: Grilled corn rolled in butter, salt and smoked paprika.
s.how: Boil 4 corn cobs for 5 minutes, then char on a hot grill for 5 minutes, turning. Cut each cob in half. Roll in 40g softened butter and sprinkle with sea salt flakes and 1 tsp smoked paprika.

s.note: Firm lime jelly cut into jagged green crystals with cream.
s.how: Make 2 packets of lime jelly crystals with 400ml boiling water instead of the usual amount, adding 2 softened gelatine leaves to set it firm. Pour into a lined slab tin and chill 4 hours. Cut into jagged crystal shards, pile on a plate and serve with 200ml whipped thickened cream.

m.note: Buttermilk fried chicken with mashed potato and gravy.
m.how: Soak 1.2kg chicken pieces overnight in 500ml buttermilk with 2 tsp salt. Dredge in 200g flour seasoned with paprika and pepper and fry at 165C for 12 to 15 minutes until 74C inside. Boil 800g potatoes, mash with butter and milk. Make gravy with 2 tbsp of the fat, 2 tbsp flour and 400ml chicken stock.

w.note: Tall crystal-shaped meringues dusted with edible glitter.
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites and 220g caster sugar in a bowl over simmering water until the sugar dissolves, then whisk off the heat with 1/4 tsp cream of tartar until stiff and glossy. Pipe tall jagged crystal shapes on lined trays and bake at 100C for 90 minutes. Cool in the oven and dust with edible glitter.

d.note: Drip coffee with milk and sugar in newsroom mugs.
d.how: Brew 1 litre of drip coffee with 60g ground coffee. Pour into four big mugs and put 200ml warm milk and a bowl of sugar on the desk so everyone fixes their own.

s.note: Warm blini with crème fraîche, salmon roe and chives.
s.how: Warm 16 buckwheat blini at 180C for 5 minutes. Top each with a teaspoon of crème fraîche, half a teaspoon of salmon roe and snipped chives. Serve straight away on a silver tray.

s.note: Devilled eggs whipped with mayo, mustard and cayenne.
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Halve and whip the yolks with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, a pinch of cayenne and 1 tsp pickle juice until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika.

m.note: Seared scotch fillet in a brandy, mustard and cream pan sauce.
m.how: Flatten 4 scotch fillet steaks, about 800g, and sear hot for 2 minutes a side, then rest. In the same pan, soften 2 chopped shallots and 1 garlic clove in 30g butter, add 60ml brandy and flame. Stir in 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 150ml beef stock and 150ml cream and reduce 4 minutes. Return the steaks to coat.

w.note: Crisp pavlova with pink raspberry cream.
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to soft peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Fold in 1 tsp cornflour and 1 tsp white vinegar, spread into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Whip 300ml thickened cream and fold through 125g crushed raspberries. Pile on top just before serving.

d.note: Brut champagne chilled hard and poured into coupes.
d.how: Chill one 750ml bottle of brut champagne to about 7C, around 3 hours in the fridge or 30 minutes in an ice bucket. Pour into four coupes, about 180ml each.

s.note: Slow-stirred creamy grits finished with butter and sharp cheddar.
s.how: Bring 500ml milk and 500ml water to the boil with 1 tsp salt. Whisk in 150g stone-ground grits or polenta, then stir over low heat for 25 minutes until creamy. Finish with 40g butter and 80g grated sharp cheddar. Not five minutes, whatever anyone says.

s.note: Cornmeal-crusted green tomatoes with a caper remoulade.
s.how: Slice 3 green tomatoes 1cm thick, salt and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry. Dip in 150ml buttermilk, then 120g fine cornmeal seasoned with salt and pepper, and shallow-fry at 180C for 2 minutes a side. Mix 100g mayonnaise, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tbsp chopped capers and a dash of hot sauce for the remoulade.

m.note: Crisp pounded steaks under black pepper cream gravy, with mash.
m.how: Pound 4 minute steaks, about 600g, very thin. Dredge in seasoned flour, dip in 200ml buttermilk, then flour again, and shallow-fry 3 minutes a side until crisp. Pour off most of the oil, stir 2 tbsp flour into the pan, whisk in 400ml milk and simmer thick with lots of black pepper. Serve over 800g mashed potato.

w.note: Classic pecan pie in crisp shortcrust.
w.how: Line a 23cm tin with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust pastry and blind bake at 180C for 15 minutes. Whisk 3 eggs, 200ml golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 60g melted butter, fold in 200g pecans and pour into the case. Bake at 170C for 45 minutes until just set. Cool before slicing.

d.note: Strong sweet black tea served cold with lemon.
d.how: Steep 6 black tea bags in 1 litre of just-boiled water for 5 minutes, remove the bags and stir in 150g caster sugar while hot. Add 500ml cold water and chill. Serve over ice with lemon slices.

s.note: Tender squid rings in a light semolina crust with lemon.
s.how: Slice 500g squid tubes into rings and soak in 250ml buttermilk for 30 minutes. Mix 100g fine semolina and 100g plain flour with plenty of salt. Toss the drained squid through and fry at 190C in batches for 90 seconds. Salt and serve with 2 lemons cut into wedges.

s.note: Fried mozzarella sandwiches in a golden egg and crumb coat.
s.how: Cut the crusts off 8 slices white bread and make 4 sandwiches with 250g sliced mozzarella. Cut each into triangles. Dip in 3 eggs beaten with 3 tbsp milk, then press into 100g breadcrumbs. Shallow-fry in 1cm of oil for 2 minutes a side until golden and the cheese melts.

m.note: Crumbed veal under marinara and bubbling mozzarella, with spaghetti.
m.how: Dust 600g veal escalopes in flour, dip in 2 beaten eggs and coat in 120g breadcrumbs. Shallow-fry 2 minutes a side until golden. Top each with warm passata, 200g sliced mozzarella and 30g parmesan and grill until bubbling. Serve with 400g spaghetti tossed in the rest of the 700ml passata.

w.note: Ricotta and orange cannoli with chocolate-dipped ends.
w.how: Drain 500g fresh ricotta for 2 hours, then beat with 80g icing sugar and the zest of 1 orange. Melt 50g dark chocolate and dip the ends of 8 cannoli shells, then let set. Pipe the filling in just before serving.

d.note: Gin, bitter red aperitif and sweet vermouth over a big cube.
d.how: For each drink, stir 30ml gin, 30ml bitter red aperitif and 30ml sweet vermouth over ice for 20 seconds and strain over a big ice cube in a tumbler. Add a slice of orange. Makes four with 120ml of each.

s.note: Salami, mortadella and provolone with capsicum, artichokes and torn bread.
s.how: Arrange 100g salami, 100g mortadella and 150g provolone on a board. Add 2 roasted red capsicums cut into strips and 200g marinated artichokes. Tear a loaf of seeded Italian bread at the table.

s.note: Pizza dough knots baked golden and tossed in garlic butter and parmesan.
s.how: Cut 500g pizza dough into 12 strips, tie each into a knot and prove 30 minutes. Bake at 230C for 12 minutes. Melt 50g butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves and chopped parsley and toss the hot knots through, then shower with 30g grated parmesan.

m.note: Seared veal in a marsala and mushroom sauce finished with butter.
m.how: Dust 600g veal escalopes with seasoned flour and sear in 20g butter and a little oil for 1 minute a side, then set aside. Brown 250g sliced button mushrooms in the pan, add 150ml marsala and 150ml beef stock and reduce by half. Whisk in 40g cold butter, return the veal and warm through.

w.note: Vanilla ricotta cannoli with mini choc chips and pistachio ends.
w.how: Drain 500g fresh ricotta for 2 hours, then beat with 80g icing sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract and 50g mini choc chips. Pipe into 8 cannoli shells just before serving and dip the ends in 30g chopped pistachios.

d.note: Chianti Classico opened early and poured into tumblers.
d.how: Open one 750ml bottle of Chianti Classico half an hour ahead and keep it at about 16C. Pour into four tumblers, about 180ml each, and keep the bottle on the table for refills during the dinner.

s.note: Corn chips baked with beans, cheddar and jalapeño, sour cream on top.
s.how: Spread 300g corn chips over a large oven tray. Scatter over a 400g tin of drained black beans, 200g grated cheddar and 2 sliced jalapeños. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes until the cheese melts. Top with 150g sour cream and 150g salsa and serve straight from the tray.

s.note: Popcorn coated in white chocolate with a pinch of flaky salt.
s.how: Pop 100g popcorn kernels in 2 tbsp oil in a large lidded pot. Melt 200g white chocolate in short bursts in the microwave and pour over the popcorn, tossing to coat. Spread on a lined tray, sprinkle with 1 tsp sea salt flakes and leave 20 minutes to set before breaking into clusters.

m.note: Slow-braised beef chuck chilli with chipotle and beans, with cornbread.
m.how: Cut 1kg beef chuck into chunks and brown in batches. Soften 2 diced brown onions and 3 garlic cloves, add 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo, 2 tsp ground cumin, 800g crushed tomatoes, a 400g tin kidney beans and the beef. Cover and braise at 160C for 2.5 hours. Bake a 350g cornbread mix as the packet says and serve alongside.

w.note: Raspberry jelly set in shallow glass dishes, fresh raspberries on top.
w.how: Soak 5 gelatine leaves in cold water for 5 minutes. Blitz 300g raspberries with 100g caster sugar and 300ml water, warm until steaming and strain. Squeeze the gelatine dry and stir into the hot purée with the juice of half a lemon. Pour into four shallow glass dishes and set in the fridge for 4 hours. Top with 125g fresh raspberries.

d.note: Blended Scotch over one big block of ice, stirred twice.
d.how: Put one large block of ice in each of four heavy tumblers. Pour 60ml blended Scotch over each, about 240ml in total. Stir twice and serve, ideally somewhere cold.

s.note: Iced prawns on sliced avocado with a lime and horseradish cocktail sauce.
s.how: Poach 500g peeled green prawns for 2 minutes in salted water, then chill in iced water. Mix 120ml tomato sauce with the juice of 1 lime, 1 tsp horseradish and a pinch of chilli flakes. Fan 2 sliced avocados across four plates, pile on the prawns and spoon over the sauce. Serve with lime wedges.

s.note: Hand-cut chips fried twice until crisp and salted straight away.
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into chips and rinse well. Fry at 140C for 6 minutes until soft but pale, drain and rest 20 minutes. Fry again at 185C for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp and golden. Salt straight away with fine salt and serve in paper cones.

m.note: Seared sirloin with red wine butter sauce and double-fried frites.
m.how: Fry 1kg potatoes cut into thin frites at 140C for 5 minutes, rest, then at 185C until crisp. Season 4 sirloin steaks, about 800g, sear hard for 3 minutes a side and rest. Sweat 2 chopped shallots in the pan fat, add 150ml red wine and reduce by two thirds, then whisk in 50g cold butter. Slice the steak and spoon the sauce over.

w.note: Vanilla ice cream with hot fudge, caramel popcorn and salted peanuts.
w.how: Pop 40g popcorn kernels. Melt 50g butter with 80g brown sugar, toss through the popcorn and bake at 150C for 10 minutes to set. Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream for hot fudge. Scoop 8 balls of vanilla ice cream into four bowls, pour over the fudge and top with the popcorn and 50g salted peanuts.

d.note: Spiced vodka and tomato juice rolled between tins, with a celery stick.
d.how: For each drink, put 45ml vodka, 120ml tomato juice, 10ml lemon juice, 2 dashes Worcestershire sauce, 2 dashes hot sauce and a pinch each of celery salt and pepper in a tin with ice. Pour back and forth between two tins 5 times, strain over fresh ice and add a celery stick. Makes four.

s.note: Rolled pizza dough spirals of pepperoni, sauce and mozzarella.
s.how: Roll 500g pizza dough into a thin rectangle. Spread with 150ml pizza sauce, cover with 80g sliced pepperoni and 150g grated mozzarella. Roll up tightly from the long side, slice into 12 rounds and place cut side up on a lined tray. Bake at 220C for 15 minutes until golden.

s.note: Cheddar, brie and gouda with crackers, grapes and honey on the brie.
s.how: Take 150g aged cheddar, 150g brie and 150g gouda out of the fridge an hour before serving. Arrange on a board with 150g crackers and a bunch of grapes. Drizzle 1 tbsp honey over the brie just before it goes on the table.

m.note: Four pizzas: pepperoni, mushroom, supreme, and everything in the fridge.
m.how: Divide 1kg pizza dough into 4 balls and stretch thin. Spread each with pizza sauce, using 400ml in total, and 400g grated mozzarella across all four. Top one with pepperoni, one with sliced mushrooms, one with pepperoni, mushroom and capsicum, and one with whatever is left. Bake each on a preheated tray at the oven's highest setting for 8 minutes.

w.note: Giant choc chip cookie baked on a pizza tray and topped with lollies.
w.how: Beat 125g soft butter with 150g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 200g plain flour, 1/2 tsp bicarb soda and 150g choc chips. Press into a greased pizza tray and bake at 180C for 15 minutes. Drizzle with 50g melted chocolate and scatter 100g lollies over the top. Cut into wedges.

d.note: Lime soda poured over vanilla ice cream until it foams.
d.how: Put two scoops of vanilla ice cream in each of four tall glasses, about 500ml in total. Slowly pour chilled lime soda over the top, about 250ml a glass, letting it foam up like ooze. Serve with a spoon and a straw.

s.note: Crustless finger sandwiches of cucumber, egg and cress, and smoked salmon.
s.how: Boil 3 eggs for 10 minutes, then mash with 2 tbsp mayonnaise and cress. Butter 12 slices white bread. Make 2 sandwiches with thin cucumber, 2 with the egg, and 2 with 100g smoked salmon on 100g cream cheese. Cut off the crusts and cut each into 3 fingers.

s.note: Crisp crumbed ricotta ravioli with warm marinara and parmesan.
s.how: Dip 400g fresh ricotta ravioli in 2 beaten eggs, then in 120g breadcrumbs. Fry at 180C in batches for 2 minutes until crisp and golden, then drain. Shower with 30g grated parmesan and serve with 300ml warm passata seasoned with salt and oregano for dipping.

m.note: Linguine in garlicky white wine clam juices with parsley.
m.how: Soak 1kg clams in salted water for 30 minutes to purge. Gently fry 4 sliced garlic cloves and a pinch of chilli in 60ml olive oil, add the clams and 150ml white wine, cover and steam 4 minutes until open. Cook 400g linguine 1 minute short, finish it in the pan juices and toss with chopped parsley and more olive oil.

w.note: Espresso-soaked biscuits layered with marsala mascarpone cream and cocoa.
w.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks with 100g caster sugar until pale, then fold in 500g mascarpone and 4 egg whites whipped stiff. Mix 300ml strong espresso with 3 tbsp marsala. Dip 24 savoiardi biscuits quickly and layer with the cream in a dish. Dust with 2 tbsp cocoa and chill overnight.

d.note: Crisp pinot grigio well chilled and poured small and often.
d.how: Chill one 750ml bottle of pinot grigio to about 8C, around 3 hours in the fridge. Pour small glasses, about 120ml each, and top up through dinner.

s.note: Quick dill pickles of cucumber and green tomato, served cold in a jar.
s.how: Slice 3 Lebanese cucumbers and 2 green tomatoes and pack into a jar with 2 sliced garlic cloves and a few dill sprigs. Heat 250ml white vinegar, 250ml water, 1 tbsp sugar and 2 tsp salt until dissolved, pour over hot and seal. Chill overnight and serve cold.

s.note: Devilled eggs whipped with mayo, mustard and cayenne, dusted with paprika.
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Halve them, whip the yolks with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp Dijon mustard and a pinch of cayenne until smooth, and pipe back into the whites. Dust with 1 tsp smoked paprika.

m.note: Beef chuck braised slowly with vegetables, stock and a splash of whiskey.
m.how: Season a 1.2kg beef chuck roast and brown all over in a heavy pot. Add 2 brown onions in wedges, 3 carrots in chunks, 500ml beef stock and 60ml Irish whiskey. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours, adding 800g halved potatoes for the last hour. Slice and serve with the juices.

w.note: Deep apple pie with sharp cheddar melted over the crust.
w.how: Peel and slice 1kg Granny Smith apples, cook 5 minutes with 80g sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon, and cool. Line a deep pie dish with 1 sheet sweet shortcrust, fill, cover with a second sheet and cut slits. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes. Lay 120g sliced sharp cheddar on top for the last 5 minutes so it melts.

d.note: Strong drip coffee poured black and refilled until the car's ready.
d.how: Brew 1 litre strong drip coffee with 70g ground coffee. Pour black into four mugs and keep the pot warm for refills. Put 100ml cream on the table for anyone who wants it.

s.note: Iced prawns on shredded lettuce with a horseradish cocktail sauce.
s.how: Poach 500g peeled green prawns for 2 minutes in salted water, then chill in iced water. Mix 120g mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp horseradish, a squeeze of lemon and a dash of hot sauce. Shred half an iceberg lettuce into four glasses, pile in the prawns and spoon the sauce over.

s.note: Little cheese cube houses with cherry tomato and gherkin trees.
s.how: Cut 120g cheddar, 120g gouda and 120g pepper jack into cubes and stack into tiny houses on a long board. Thread 250g cherry tomatoes and 100g cornichons onto toothpicks as trees between them, like Adam's model town.

m.note: Grilled lobster tails in garlic parsley butter with shoestring fries.
m.how: Split 4 lobster tails lengthways. Mash 80g soft butter with 2 crushed garlic cloves, lemon zest and chopped parsley and brush over the flesh. Grill flesh side up for 6 minutes until just opaque. Fry 800g potatoes cut into shoestrings at 180C until crisp and serve with 100g salad leaves dressed in lemon.

w.note: Black and white striped marble loaf under white chocolate ganache.
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour with 80ml milk. Stir 2 tbsp cocoa into half the batter. Pipe alternating stripes into a loaf tin and bake at 170C for 50 minutes. Melt 150g white chocolate with 60ml cream and pour over, then pipe stripes with 50g melted dark chocolate.

d.note: White rum, lime and ripe banana blended smooth with ice.
d.how: Dissolve 60g caster sugar in 60ml hot water and cool. For four drinks, blend 180ml white rum, 80ml lime juice, 60ml syrup and 2 ripe bananas with 4 cups of ice until smooth. Pour into chilled glasses.

s.note: Creamy clam and potato chowder with bacon and oyster crackers.
s.how: Fry 150g diced bacon until crisp, then sweat 1 diced onion and 2 celery sticks in the fat. Add 400g diced potatoes, 500ml clam juice or fish stock and thyme and simmer 15 minutes. Stir in 250g chopped clam meat and 200ml cream for the last 3 minutes. Serve in cups with 100g oyster crackers.

s.note: Double-fried chips with malt vinegar and salt in paper cones.
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into chips, rinse and dry. Fry at 140C for 6 minutes until soft, rest 20 minutes, then fry at 185C until crisp. Salt well, splash with 3 tbsp malt vinegar and serve in paper cones.

m.note: Lager-battered flathead with chips, minted mushy peas and malt vinegar.
m.how: Whisk 200g plain flour, 50g cornflour and 330ml ice-cold lager into a batter. Dust 800g flathead fillets in flour, dip and fry at 180C for 4 minutes. Fry 1kg potatoes as chips at 140C then 185C. Cook 400g frozen peas, crush with butter and mint. Serve with malt vinegar.

w.note: Two sponge layers filled with vanilla custard under dark chocolate ganache.
w.how: Whisk 4 eggs and 120g sugar until thick, fold in 120g flour and bake in two 20cm tins at 180C for 18 minutes. For custard, heat 300ml milk, whisk into 3 yolks, 60g sugar and 25g cornflour and cook until thick, then cool. Sandwich the sponges with custard. Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream and pour over the top.

d.note: Cranberry juice over ice, with vodka if you need to keep your cover.
d.how: Fill four short glasses with ice and pour 150ml cranberry juice into each. For anyone keeping their cover, add 30ml vodka, about 120ml for four.

s.note: Corn chips with beans and jalapeño under a spiderweb of hot queso.
s.how: Spread 300g corn chips on a tray with a 400g tin black beans and 2 sliced jalapeños and warm at 180C for 5 minutes. Melt 200g grated cheddar into 150ml evaporated milk over low heat, stirring until smooth. Pour into a squeeze bottle and pipe a spiderweb across the chips.

s.note: Mini rolls of roast turkey, cranberry sauce and crisp stuffing.
s.how: Make a 170g stuffing mix as the packet says, press into a tray and bake at 190C for 25 minutes until crisp, then cut into 8 squares. Toast 8 slider buns. Fill each with 300g warm sliced roast turkey in total, a spoon of cranberry sauce and a square of stuffing.

m.note: Brined roast turkey breast with stuffing, gravy, potato and pumpkin.
m.how: Brine a 1.2kg turkey breast overnight in 2 litres water with 100g salt. Pat dry, rub with butter and roast at 170C to 70C inside, about 75 minutes. Rest 15 minutes. Roast 800g potatoes and 600g pumpkin in chunks alongside. Bake a 170g stuffing mix. Make gravy from the pan juices, 2 tbsp flour and 400ml chicken stock.

w.note: Fluffy buttermilk pancakes stacked high and drowned in maple syrup.
w.how: Whisk 250g plain flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder and a pinch of salt. Add 2 eggs, 400ml buttermilk and 40g melted butter and rest 15 minutes. Cook ladlefuls in a buttered pan over medium heat until bubbles set, then flip. Stack high and pour over 150ml maple syrup.

d.note: Red and blue cordial slush layered in one cup.
d.how: Blend 100ml raspberry cordial with 2 cups ice and 100ml water until slushy, and do the same with 100ml blue cordial. Spoon the red into four cups, then layer the blue on top. Serve with a spoon straw.

s.n: Rye toast with chicken liver pâté
s.note: Silky brandy chicken liver pâté under clarified butter, on rye toast.
s.how: Trim 400g chicken livers and sear in butter for 2 minutes a side until still pink. Add 2 chopped shallots and thyme, then 40ml brandy and let it bubble off. Blitz with 150g soft butter until silky, season and press into a dish. Pour over 50g melted clarified butter and chill 4 hours. Serve with 8 slices toasted rye.

s.note: Twisted puff pastry straws with cheddar, parmesan and cayenne.
s.how: Brush 2 sheets puff pastry with 1 beaten egg. Scatter one sheet with 80g grated aged cheddar, 30g grated parmesan and a pinch of cayenne, lay the other on top and press. Cut into 1.5cm strips, twist each and bake at 220C for 12 minutes until puffed and golden.

m.note: Lamb neck chops braised with potato, onion, carrot and stout.
m.how: Brown 1.2kg lamb neck chops in batches. Layer in a heavy pot with 2 sliced brown onions, 3 carrots in chunks and 800g potatoes in thick slices. Pour over 375ml stout and 300ml beef stock, cover and braise at 160C for 2 hours until tender. Finish with chopped parsley.

w.note: Brioche and whiskey-soaked raisin pudding baked in a rich custard.
w.how: Soak 80g raisins in 60ml Irish whiskey for 30 minutes. Butter 8 slices stale brioche and layer in a dish with the raisins. Whisk 4 eggs, 300ml milk, 200ml cream and 80g sugar and pour over. Rest 30 minutes, then bake at 170C for 40 minutes until puffed and golden.

d.note: Irish whiskey neat in a heavy glass, water on the side.
d.how: Pour 45ml Irish whiskey into each of four heavy glasses, about 180ml in total. Put a small jug of cold water on the table for anyone who wants a few drops.

s.note: Pizza dough knots tossed hot in garlic butter, parsley and parmesan.
s.how: Cut 500g pizza dough into 12 strips, tie each into a knot and prove 30 minutes. Bake at 230C for 12 minutes until golden. Melt 50g butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves and chopped parsley, toss the hot knots through and shower with 30g grated parmesan.

s.note: Ice-cold watermelon with chilli, lime and salt at the table.
s.how: Chill a quarter watermelon, about 2kg, for several hours. Cut into wedges. Mix 1 tsp sea salt flakes, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes and the zest of 1 lime in a little bowl and sprinkle over at the table, with lime wedges to squeeze.

m.note: Big thin New York slices with mozzarella, pepperoni and oregano.
m.how: Rest 2 balls of pizza dough, about 500g, at room temperature for an hour. Season 400g crushed tomatoes with salt and stretch the bases thin. Spread with sauce, top with 250g grated low-moisture mozzarella and 100g pepperoni and bake on a preheated tray at the oven's highest setting for 8 to 10 minutes. Sprinkle with oregano and cut big.

w.note: Crushed ice soaked with homemade cherry syrup.
w.how: Simmer 300g cherries, pitted, with 150g caster sugar, 150ml water and the juice of 1 lemon for 10 minutes, then strain and cool the syrup. Shave or crush 1kg ice into four cups and pour the syrup over just before serving.

d.note: American lager frozen cold, straight from the bottle.
d.how: Put four 355ml bottles of American lager in the freezer for 25 minutes, no longer, so they are ice cold but not frozen. Serve straight from the bottle on a hot night.

s.note: Kettle chips with a bright green herb, garlic and lemon dip.
s.how: Blitz 200g sour cream, 100g cream cheese, 1 garlic clove, the juice of half a lemon, a big handful of parsley and a bunch of chives until green and smooth. Season with salt and chill 30 minutes. Serve with 300g kettle chips.

s.note: Chocolate-tipped pretzel rods set in groups of five with flaky salt.
s.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate in short bursts. Dip the tips of 20 pretzel rods, lay them on baking paper in groups of five like fingers and sprinkle each tip with a pinch of sea salt flakes. Leave 20 minutes to set.

m.note: Beef chuck chilli with chipotle and cocoa, under sour cream and cheddar.
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 2 diced brown onions and 3 garlic cloves, add 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tbsp cocoa, 800g crushed tomatoes, a 400g tin kidney beans and the beef. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours until thick. Serve topped with 150g sour cream and 100g grated cheddar.

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes piped with red and green striped buttercream.
w.how: Beat 125g soft butter with 150g caster sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 100ml milk. Spoon into 12 cases and bake at 175C for 18 minutes. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar, split in two and colour one red and one green. Spoon both side by side into one piping bag and pipe swirls.

d.note: Strong plunger coffee served black in big mugs.
d.how: Put 60g ground coffee in a large plunger, pour over 1 litre of just-off-the-boil water and steep 4 minutes. Plunge and pour into four big mugs. Serve black, with 100ml milk on the side for anyone who isn't trying to stay awake.

s.note: Buttery rosemary nuts with chocolate almonds and pretzels.
s.how: Melt 30g butter with 2 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tbsp chopped rosemary. Toss through 300g mixed nuts, spread on a tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring once. Cool, then mix with 150g chocolate almonds and 100g pretzels.

s.note: Toasted English muffins with pizza sauce and bubbling mozzarella.
s.how: Split 4 English muffins and toast lightly. Spread each half with pizza sauce, using 150ml in total, and top with 150g grated mozzarella. Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling and spotted brown. Cut into halves to serve.

m.note: Macaroni in Gruyère cheese sauce with butter-poached lobster and crumbs.
m.how: Gently poach the meat of 2 lobster tails in 40g butter for 4 minutes and chop. Melt 40g butter, stir in 40g flour, then whisk in 600ml warm milk and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in 120g grated Gruyère and 100g cheddar. Fold through 400g cooked macaroni and the lobster, tip into a dish, top with 40g panko mixed with 20g melted butter and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

w.note: Towering sundae with hot fudge, cream, nuts, sprinkles and a cherry.
w.how: Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml thickened cream for hot fudge. Whip another 200ml cream. Pile 8 scoops vanilla ice cream into four tall glasses, pour over the fudge, add the cream, 40g chopped nuts, sprinkles and a maraschino cherry on each.

d.note: Rich hot chocolate topped with whipped cream and marshmallows.
d.how: Heat 1 litre full cream milk until steaming and whisk in 150g chopped dark chocolate until smooth. Pour into four mugs, top with 150ml whipped thickened cream and a handful of marshmallows.

s.note: Soft salted pretzels with yellow mustard, like a subway stall.
s.how: Mix 500g bread flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tsp salt and 300ml warm water, knead 8 minutes and rise 1 hour. Shape 8 pretzels. Dip each for 30 seconds in 2 litres simmering water with 4 tbsp bicarb soda, sprinkle with rock salt and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve with 100g yellow mustard.

s.note: Warm jam doughnuts rolled in caster sugar.
s.how: Warm 8 jam doughnuts on a tray at 160C for 2 minutes. Roll each straight away in 80g caster sugar so it sticks, and serve on a plate in the middle of the table like the transit office tray.

m.note: Long turkey, Swiss and salad heroes wrapped tight in paper.
m.how: Split 4 long rolls and spread each with mayonnaise, using 100g in total. Layer with 400g sliced turkey, 8 slices Swiss cheese, shredded iceberg lettuce and 2 sliced tomatoes. Season, close, wrap tightly in paper and cut in half.

w.note: Butter cake under a thick layer of cinnamon crumble.
w.how: Rub 100g flour, 100g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 80g cold butter into big crumbs. Beat 125g butter with 125g caster sugar, add 2 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour with 100ml milk. Spread in a lined 20cm square tin, cover thickly with the crumble and bake at 180C for 40 minutes.

d.note: Drip coffee with milk and sugar in paper cups.
d.how: Brew 1 litre of drip coffee with 60g ground coffee. Pour into four paper cups, add milk, about 200ml in total, and sugar to taste, and snap on the lids.

s.note: Warm crusty Italian loaf torn into grassy olive oil and salt.
s.how: Warm a crusty Italian loaf at 200C for 8 minutes. Pour 80ml extra virgin olive oil into a shallow dish with 1 tsp sea salt flakes and a good crack of pepper. Tear the bread at the table and dip.

s.note: Fried eggs cooked in rings of red capsicum inside buttered toast.
s.how: Cut a hole in 4 thick slices white bread. Melt 40g butter in a big pan and lay in the bread. Put a thick ring of red capsicum in each hole, crack an egg into it, and fry until the white sets, flipping the bread once. Season with salt and pepper.

m.note: Thin seared chicken in lemon, white wine and caper butter sauce.
m.how: Slice 2 large chicken breasts, about 600g, in half horizontally and pound thin. Dust in flour and sear in oil and 20g butter for 2 minutes a side, then set aside. Add 100ml white wine, the juice of 1 lemon and 2 tbsp capers, reduce by half and swirl in 40g cold butter and parsley. Return the chicken to coat.

w.note: Orange ricotta cannoli with chocolate-dipped ends.
w.how: Drain 500g fresh ricotta for 2 hours, then beat with 80g icing sugar and the zest of 1 orange. Dip the ends of 8 cannoli shells in 50g melted dark chocolate and let set. Pipe in the filling just before serving.

d.note: Brut champagne in coupes for the family toast at the end.
d.how: Chill one 750ml bottle of brut champagne to about 7C. Pour into four coupes, about 180ml each, and raise them to la famiglia, the way they do at the kitchen table.

s.note: Popcorn tossed in hot maple butter caramel and set into clusters.
s.how: Pop 80g popcorn kernels in 2 tbsp oil. Boil 200ml maple syrup with 40g butter to 120C, about 6 minutes. Pour over the popcorn, toss fast with two spoons, spread on a lined tray and leave 20 minutes to set. Break into clusters.

s.note: Pretzel rods dipped in white chocolate and crushed candy canes.
s.how: Melt 200g white chocolate in short bursts. Crush 6 candy canes in a bag with a rolling pin. Dip 20 pretzel rods two thirds into the chocolate, roll straight away in the candy cane and lay on baking paper to set.

m.note: Spaghetti in maple butter, chocolate sauce, marshmallows and lollies.
m.how: Cook 400g spaghetti and drain. Toss with 40g butter and 100ml maple syrup. Pile into four bowls, drizzle with 100ml chocolate sauce and top with 80g marshmallows and a handful of crushed lollies. Serve as dinner, the way Buddy would.

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes domed in cream cheese frosting and coconut.
w.how: Beat 125g soft butter with 150g caster sugar, add 2 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour with 100ml milk. Bake in 12 cases at 180C for 18 minutes and cool. Beat 250g cream cheese with 50g butter and 250g icing sugar, dome thickly on each cake and roll in 80g shredded coconut.

d.note: Strong drip coffee with sugar and milk on the table.
d.how: Brew 1 litre strong drip coffee with 70g ground coffee. Pour into four mugs and put 200ml milk and a bowl of sugar on the table, with a sign saying it is the world's best.

s.note: Crunchy smoked paprika peanuts in little bowls on the bar.
s.how: Whisk 1 egg white until frothy, then stir in 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp caster sugar. Toss through 300g peanuts, spread on a lined tray and roast at 160C for 15 minutes, stirring once, until crisp. Cool and serve in small bowls.

s.note: Thin homemade crisps with salt and malt vinegar.
s.how: Slice 600g potatoes paper thin on a mandoline, rinse well and dry completely. Fry at 170C in small batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain, sprinkle with sea salt flakes and splash with 2 tbsp malt vinegar.

m.note: Steak and ale pie with chips and mushy peas.
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then soften 2 sliced brown onions. Add 330ml English ale, 300ml beef stock and 2 tbsp flour stirred in first, cover and braise at 160C for 2.5 hours. Cool slightly, tip into a pie dish, cover with 1 sheet puff pastry and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 1kg chips and 400g frozen peas cooked and crushed.

w.note: Date sponge drowned in warm toffee sauce with cream.
w.how: Soak 200g chopped dates in 250ml boiling water with 1 tsp bicarb soda for 10 minutes. Beat 80g butter with 150g brown sugar, add 2 eggs, fold in 180g self-raising flour and the dates. Bake in a greased dish at 180C for 30 minutes. Simmer 100g butter, 150g brown sugar and 200ml cream for 3 minutes and pour over. Serve with cream.

d.note: English ale or lager poured into pint glasses for a toast.
d.how: Chill four 500ml cans or bottles of English ale, or lager for anyone who prefers it. Pour into pint glasses at a tilt so the head settles, and raise them to the Winchester.

s.note: Toasted bagels with cream cheese, lox, capers, onion and dill.
s.how: Split and toast 4 bagels. Spread each half thickly with cream cheese, using 200g in total. Top with 200g smoked salmon, 1 tbsp capers, thinly sliced red onion and small sprigs of dill. Cut each half in two to share.

s.note: Bakery soft pretzels refreshed with butter and salt, mustard alongside.
s.how: Brush 4 soft pretzels with 20g melted butter and sprinkle with 1 tsp rock salt. Bake at 200C for 5 minutes until hot and glossy. Cut in half and serve with 100g yellow mustard.

m.note: Steamed pastrami heroes with Swiss, coleslaw and Russian dressing.
m.how: Steam 500g sliced pastrami for 10 minutes until glossy. Mix 100g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp horseradish and 1 tbsp chopped pickle for Russian dressing. Toss 250g coleslaw mix with half the dressing. Fill 4 long rolls with pastrami, 8 slices Swiss cheese, the slaw and the rest of the dressing.

w.note: Soft vanilla cookies iced half vanilla, half chocolate.
w.how: Beat 115g butter with 150g caster sugar, add 1 egg, 80g sour cream and 1 tsp vanilla, then mix in 250g plain flour and 1 tsp baking powder. Scoop 12 mounds onto lined trays and bake at 180C for 12 minutes. Make a thick icing with 250g icing sugar and hot water, ice half of each flat side, then add 2 tbsp cocoa to the rest and ice the other half.

d.note: Drip coffee in thick mugs, paid for before you drink it.
d.how: Brew 1 litre of drip coffee with 60g ground coffee. Pour into four thick mugs with 200ml milk on the side. Pay for it first, the way Serpico always did.

s.note: Soy, honey and sesame roasted nuts and pumpkin seeds.
s.how: Toss 250g mixed nuts and 50g pumpkin seeds with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey and 1 tbsp sesame seeds. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring once. Cool on the tray so they crisp.

s.note: Salted edamame with a drop of sesame oil.
s.how: Boil 500g frozen edamame in salted water for 4 minutes and drain well. Toss with 1 tsp sea salt flakes and 1 tsp sesame oil and serve warm in a bowl, with another bowl for the empty pods.

m.note: Glazed teriyaki chicken over rice with pickled ginger and spring onion.
m.how: Simmer 80ml soy sauce, 80ml mirin, 60ml sake and 2 tbsp sugar for 5 minutes until syrupy. Sear 800g chicken thighs skin side down for 8 minutes, flip, cook 5 minutes, then pour in the sauce and turn until glazed. Slice over 400g steamed short grain rice with 40g pickled ginger and sliced spring onion.

w.note: Creamy coconut ice cream scattered with golden toasted coconut.
w.how: Toast 50g shredded coconut in a dry pan until golden. Blend 400ml coconut cream, 200ml thickened cream and 120g caster sugar until the sugar dissolves, then stir in most of the coconut. Churn, or freeze in a tub and stir every hour for 4 hours. Scoop and finish with the rest of the coconut.

d.note: Sencha steeped gently and poured into small cups.
d.how: Heat 800ml water to about 75C, just steaming. Pour over 2 tbsp sencha green tea in a small pot and steep 90 seconds. Pour into four small cups, going back and forth so each cup gets an even strength.

s.note: Saffron risotto balls with mozzarella and peas, fried deep gold.
s.how: Cook 300g arborio rice in 900ml stock with a pinch of saffron until thick and chill overnight on a tray. Wrap golf balls of rice around a cube of mozzarella and a few peas, using 100g mozzarella and 50g peas. Roll in flour, 2 beaten eggs and 100g breadcrumbs, and fry at 175C until deep gold.

s.note: Prosciutto, lemony bresaola with rocket, eggplant, capsicum and olives.
s.how: Lay 100g prosciutto flat on a board. Dress 100g bresaola with lemon juice, olive oil and a handful of rocket. Add 150g marinated eggplant, 2 roasted red capsicums peeled and sliced, 150g mixed olives and a warm loaf of Italian bread.

m.note: Pasta drum of ziti, ragù, salami, egg and provolone, cut like a cake.
m.how: Make dough with 300g 00 flour and 3 eggs, roll thin and line a buttered ovenproof bowl. Toss 400g cooked ziti with ragù made from 500g beef mince and 700ml passata. Layer in the bowl with 100g diced salami, 3 boiled eggs and 150g provolone. Fold the dough over, bake at 180C for 1 hour, rest 30 minutes, turn out and slice.

w.note: Vanilla panna cotta turned out with fresh berries.
w.how: Soak 2 gelatine leaves in cold water. Heat 500ml thickened cream, 100ml milk, 80g caster sugar and a split vanilla bean until steaming. Squeeze the gelatine and whisk it in, strain, and pour into four moulds. Set 6 hours. Dip the moulds in hot water, turn out and serve with 250g berries.

d.note: Lightly chilled grappa in small glasses, with espresso for the brave.
d.how: Chill a bottle of grappa for an hour. Pour 30ml into each of four small glasses, about 120ml in total. Make four short espressos with 30g ground coffee for anyone still standing after the timpano.

s.note: Crustless ham and Swiss quarters with mustard butter, wrapped in wax paper.
s.how: Mash 40g soft butter with 1 tsp Dijon mustard and spread over 8 slices white bread. Fill with 200g leg ham and 4 slices Swiss cheese. Cut off the crusts, cut into quarters and wrap in wax paper, like the automat windows.

s.note: Simmered franks with mustard and caraway sauerkraut in steamed buns.
s.how: Simmer 8 hot dog franks with half a sliced onion for 5 minutes. Warm 300g sauerkraut with 1 tsp caraway seeds. Steam 8 hot dog buns for a minute, add a frank to each, top with sauerkraut and a line of yellow mustard, using 4 tbsp.

m.note: Crunchy coconut prawns with sweet chilli and lime.
m.how: Butterfly 600g green prawns, leaving the tails on. Dust in 50g flour, dip in 2 beaten eggs, then press into 80g panko mixed with 80g shredded coconut. Fry at 180C for 2 minutes until golden. Serve with 150ml sweet chilli sauce and lime wedges.

w.note: Whole boiled orange and almond cake, moist and fragrant.
w.how: Boil 2 whole oranges for 1 hour until soft, cool and blitz smooth, skin and all. Beat 6 eggs with 250g caster sugar, then mix in the oranges, 250g almond meal and 1 tsp baking powder. Pour into a lined 22cm tin and bake at 180C for 1 hour. Cool in the tin.

d.note: Drip coffee with milk and two sugars in thick mugs.
d.how: Brew 1 litre of drip coffee with 50g ground coffee. Pour into four thick mugs with a splash of milk, about 150ml in total, and two sugars in each.
